summary: Iteration 7 — verified the new PWA + Web Push wiring end-to-end. New pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_pwa_push.py (13 tests, all pass) covers the static PWA assets (/manifest.json, /sw.js, /icons/icon-192.png, /icons/icon-512.png, /icons/apple-touch-icon.png) and the push endpoints (GET /api/push/vapid-public-key → {enabled:true}, POST /api/push/subscribe stores subs / requires auth / rejects missing endpoint, POST /api/push/test → {sent:true}, POST /api/push/unsubscribe removes sub, and a broadcast to a cadet with an intentionally unreachable subscription does NOT crash — graceful pywebpush handling verified). Full backend suite is now 123/123 passing (previous 110 + 13 new). Playwright verified: service worker registers on /portal load (navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations().length === 1), <link rel='manifest'> is present, cadet login → notice-ack gate cleared → PWA banner [data-testid='pwa-banner'] renders at top of dashboard with 'Turn on notifications' button [pwa-notify-btn] and 'X' dismiss [pwa-dismiss] (install button [pwa-install-btn] is correctly absent in headless Chromium — no beforeinstallprompt, no iOS). Dismiss works: banner disappears and localStorage 'pwa_banner_dismissed'==='1'. All 8 portal tabs (calendar, points, notices, documents, news, inbox, messages, account) navigate cleanly with no errors — regression clean. Inbox correctly showed the TEST_pwa_push_broadcast delivered from the pytest run (proves push_to_user path did not crash even with an unreachable fake subscription in the DB). ONE FRONTEND BUG found: enablePush() and turnOnNotifications() have no try/catch around navigator.serviceWorker.ready → pushManager.subscribe(), so when the underlying browser Push service refuses (e.g. headless/incognito Chromium: 'Registration failed - permission denied'), an uncaught runtime error propagates instead of the intended toast.error(...). In dev this surfaces as the CRA error overlay; in production the click silently does nothing (no toast, no state update). Real browsers on real user devices will normally succeed, but any failure path is currently swallowed as an unhandled promise rejection — needs a try/catch that maps the exception to res={ok:false,reason:'error'}.

minor.issue: PushSubscription pydantic model only validates {'subscription': dict} — the inner subscription is accepted as any dict. Consider a nested model with required 'endpoint' + 'keys.p256dh' + 'keys.auth' so bad clients get a clean 422 instead of a 400 with 'Invalid subscription'.

No per-user cap on stored subscriptions. A misbehaving client could upsert unlimited endpoints (one per (endpoint) key). Recommend limiting subscriptions per user_id to e.g. 10 with LRU-eviction, or capping total stored subs.

ui_bugs.issue: enablePush() does not wrap navigator.serviceWorker.ready → pushManager.subscribe() in try/catch. If the browser refuses (e.g. incognito, or user later revokes permission, or Chrome push service is offline), the promise rejects and turnOnNotifications() (which awaits enablePush() without try/catch either) propagates an unhandled rejection. Users see nothing in production; in dev the CRA overlay 'Uncaught runtime errors: Registration failed - permission denied' appears. Should wrap in try/catch and return {ok:false, reason:'error'} so the existing toast.error('This device or browser doesn't support notifications.') fires.

action_items: FRONTEND (MEDIUM): Add try/catch inside pwa.js::enablePush() around Notification.requestPermission / serviceWorker.ready / pushManager.subscribe / api.post('/push/subscribe'), returning {ok:false, reason:'error'} on any thrown error, and likewise wrap turnOnNotifications in PwaManager. This eliminates the 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay when Push is unavailable and shows the intended toast.error to the user.
OPTIONAL (backend, minor): tighten the PushSubscription pydantic model to a nested schema so bad clients get a clean 422.
OPTIONAL (backend, minor): cap push_subscriptions per user_id (e.g. 10 with LRU-eviction).
PRE-EXISTING (still open from iterations 3-6): server.py is now 1679 lines — split into routers is overdue. The new push endpoints are cleanly extractable to routers/push.py.
critical_code_review_comments: pwa.js::enablePush() lacks try/catch — a pushManager.subscribe failure is an unhandled promise rejection today (CRA dev overlay). See action_items.

server.py::_send_one_push() catches WebPushException and deletes 404/410 subs — good. But asyncio.to_thread(_send_one_push, ...) is fired one-at-a-time inside push_to_user's for-loop; for a broadcast to N cadets each with M subs this is N*M sequential HTTPS round-trips (webpush to FCM/Apple). Consider asyncio.gather(...) so pushes fan out in parallel (still bounded — max 20 subs per user by design).

The service worker (public/sw.js) writes badge from data.badge but push_to_user() never puts a 'badge' key into the payload — so setAppBadge from the SW never fires on push. Badge is only refreshed from Dashboard via /notifications/unread-count. Consider adding badge=unread_count to the push payload when generated inside push_to_user so installed PWAs on Chrome-desktop get an accurate badge without needing the app open.
PushSubscription pydantic model accepts any dict for 'subscription' — no schema enforcement of endpoint/keys. Not a security issue (auth required) but a data-hygiene one.
public/manifest.json declares 3 icons — /icons/icon-192.png, /icons/icon-512.png (both purpose:any) and /icons/icon-maskable-512.png (maskable). Both returned 200. Good.

public/sw.js does not scope by version or clean up outdated caches — that's fine today because it doesn't cache anything (only push+notificationclick handlers). If a future iteration adds cache-first offline for /portal, add a version constant and skipWaiting/clean-caches pattern.

Full suite: test_backend.py + test_phase2.py + test_portal.py + test_recruit_email.py + test_attachments_and_buckets.py + test_documents_blogs_calendar.py + test_pwa_push.py = 123 tests, all passing. Run: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://raf-horwich.preview.emergentagent.com python -m pytest backend/tests/ -v (~2m). Playwright tips for this feature: (1) do NOT pre-grant notifications with context.grant_permissions() because Notification.permission then becomes 'granted' and canPrompt=false → banner hides; (2) instead use context.add_init_script to spoof Notification.permission getter to 'default' and Notification.requestPermission to return 'granted'; (3) install button [pwa-install-btn] will NOT appear in headless Chromium (no beforeinstallprompt fires, no iOS UA) — that's expected. Data-testids exercised: pwa-banner, pwa-notify-btn, pwa-install-btn (absent in headless), pwa-dismiss, tab-inbox, tab-calendar/points/notices/documents/news/messages/account, notice-ack-<id>. Known limitation of headless Chromium: navigator.serviceWorker.ready.pushManager.subscribe() throws 'Registration failed - permission denied' because Chromium built for headless treats Push API as incognito — so the actual end-to-end subscribe call cannot be validated in the automation harness; wiring is instead validated at the API layer (POST /api/push/subscribe with a fake body).
rca of the issue: The frontend uncaught runtime error 'Registration failed - permission denied' originates from pushManager.subscribe() throwing when the underlying browser Push service is unavailable (typical in Playwright headless Chromium which behaves like incognito for Push API purposes — see https://crbug.com/401439 logged in console). Because pwa.js::enablePush() and PwaManager::turnOnNotifications() do not wrap the call in try/catch, the rejection escapes as an unhandled promise rejection, caught only by React's dev-mode error overlay. Mitigation: wrap both in try/catch returning {ok:false, reason:'error'} so the existing toast.error branch fires and the user gets clear feedback. This will not affect real-browser users where subscribe succeeds, but it will improve UX in edge cases (private browsing, corporate networks blocking FCM/APNs, permission revoked mid-session).
